evidence.note: CONFIRMED: before the fix, a cycle where the victim holds two leases in the waiter's way made autoorder._candidates order only ('T2','T1') and propose return one edge, and health._cycle_locks returned LOCKED only for the waiter item, missing the second dropped lease. Cheap test = AO.propose with victim blockers ['T2','T4'] -> edges [('T2','T1')] (bug) then [('T2','T1'),('T4','T1')] (fixed); H.inspect over the alpha/beta cycle -> ['alpha','beta','check','docs'] locked items.

autoorder._victim_items() + _candidates() order every dropped lease; propose() adds an edge per dropped item instead of stopping after the first; health._link_locks() + _cycle_locks() emit a LOCKED row for every blocking lease. chunk_findings.detail: The fixture puts the two asserted entries in `"blockers"` while the link still has only a single `"item": "check"` and no `"items"` list. The health half of B-autoorder-first-drop-only is that `_cycle_locks` reads only `link.item`, so a second *wait* of the same agent is missing; the intent says the new `Link.items` field carries those waits. This test never supplies a second wait, so a broken `_link_locks` that continues to ignore `Link.items` and merely iterates `blockers` would make this test pass, leaving the stated second-wait bug untested. The test exercises the auto-order victim-drop scenario, not the health second-wait scenario it claims to cover.

chunk_findings.detail: The “already ordered” branch still breaks after examining only the first victim candidate. If `_victim_items(cycle)` returns two dropped leases such as `["lease-A1", "lease-A2"]` and the existing needs graph already contains `lease-A1 -> lease-B` (precisely the state left by the old first-drop-only autoorder), the first candidate `("lease-A1", "lease-B")` hits `earlier in reach(later)`, sets `resolved = True`, and breaks. The loop never examines `("lease-A2", "lease-B")`, so no edge is added for the second dropped lease. That leaves the second lease able to take the files back, meaning the fix does not repair existing partially-ordered autoorder data.

chunk_findings.detail: A successful fallback edge is not recorded, so the failure note still fires. `added` is only incremented in the victim-drop loop, and the fallback `_ADDED` branch just `break`s without setting `already`. Given a cycle with no `victim_item`, agents `("Tb", "Ta")`, and one link `item="Tb"` blocked by `"Ta"` (both eligible, empty `needs`), `_take` appends `Edge("Tb", "Ta", ...)` and returns `_ADDED`, then `added == 0 and not already` is still true, so the return is `(edges=[that edge], notes=["no edge for Tb -> Ta: ..."])`. The same false note is emitted when every victim-drop pair is `_SKIP` and the fallback pair is the one that actually orders the cycle.

chunk_findings.detail: Fallback still runs after a victim drop that is already ordered. The guard is `if added == 0`, and `_ALREADY` never increments `added`. Given victim item `Ta`, links `(Tb blocked by Ta)`, `(Tc blocked by Tb)`, `(Ta blocked by Tc)`, and `needs` already containing `Ta -> Tb`, the drop pair returns `_ALREADY` (`added` stays 0, `already` becomes true) and the fallback loop still appends `Edge("Tc", "Tb", ...)`. That is an extra ordering the drop did not need; the comment says the fallback is only for when no drop could be ordered.

It returns `_blockers` of the first link that contains `victim_item`, so a second dropped lease that is only on `drops` (or on a later link) is never ordered.
